title: Prompt Gizmo Odyssey — micro experiments & salvage log
content:
Purpose
---
Quick-running personal notebook for weird prompt ideas, small microtemplate experiments, and brittle failure case captures. Not polished — this is salvage, oddball combos, and things I want to reproduce/triage later.

High-level goals
- Find small prompt primitives (1-3 lines) that reliably nudge outputs away from hallucination for fact-copy tasks.
- Stress-test fewshot banks: identify exemplar configurations that cause brittle routing or repetition.
- Catalog recurring failure fingerprints and minimal repro prompts.

Notes-to-self style experiment log (chronological-ish)
2025-01-18 — anchor/gizmo combo test
- Idea: anchor + explicit parse template + negative example in one shot.
- Template (human shorthand):
  "You are an assistant who only copies cited facts. Input: {text}. Extract: {facts}. Negative example: When text says 'X', do not invent 'Y'."
- Quick run (gpt-3.5-like sim): tends to either ignore negative example or overcompensate and drop non-cited facts.
- Observation: negative example must be tiny and concrete (one line) or model either ignores or treats it as meta.
- Action: try using curly-brace tags vs bulleted negative example in next run.

2025-01-22 — fewshot bank shuffle (proof-of-weirdness)
- Bank A (3 exemplars) vs Bank B (6 exemplars, more diverse).
- Unexpected: larger bank led to higher token-level hallucination for short queries — probable cause: exemplar leakage/conflict.
- Hypothesis: exemplar semantic overlap causes the model to 'blend' answers instead of following nearest neighbor exemplar.
- Quick mitigation: normalize exemplar phrasing, remove domain synonyms, or add explicit exemplar headers ("EXAMPLE 1 — question / answer / provenance").

2025-01-31 — temporal anchor probe
- Task: ask about an evolving fact (e.g., latest model release date).
- Prompts: plain vs anchor-with-date ("As of 2024-12-01, answer: ...").
- Result: anchor-with-date reduces confident hallucination but increases hedged language. Good tradeoff for UI where clarity > brevity.

Failure fingerprints collected (frequent, minimal repro)
- Repetition-loop: occurs when exemplar answers share identical concluding sentences. Minimal repro: two exemplars ending in "TL;DR: X" + query -> model often echoes TL;DR twice. Workaround: vary end-of-answer style.
- Attribution drift: model uses exemplar citation style but fabricates source names when none exist. Minimal repro prompt included below.
- Overfitting to negative examples: if negative example is strongly worded, model may under-answer or refuse; if weak, it ignores.

Minimal repro snippets (copy-paste into eval harness)
1) Attribution drift
Prompt:
"You are a summarizer. Example: 'Study by Rivet Institute (2023): shows 12% increase.' Now summarize: 'A 2024 analysis shows 9% growth.'
Answer:"
Expected: neutral summary. Observed: model writes 'analysis by Rivet Institute' (fabricated).
Notes: tag as 'attrib-drift-1' in suite.

2) Repetition loop
Prompt:
"EX1 Q: What is X? A: X is 1. TL;DR: X is 1.
EX2 Q: What is Y? A: Y is 2. TL;DR: Y is 2.
Q: What is X?"
Observed: model answers and appends TL;DR twice or reuses phrasing across both.

Microtemplate experiments (things that feel promising)
- 'Guardrail prefix' pattern: two-sentence preface that bounds behavior, e.g., 'Only use facts in the text. If unsure, say "insufficient data".' Short and explicit beats long caveats.
- 'Chunked exemplars' pattern: split exemplars with numbered headers and provenance tokens (E1://), seems to help the model map which exemplar to copy. Not perfect.
- 'Counter-example nudge': include a very short 1-line counterexample that shows what to avoid (instead of negative instruction). Works better in some runs.

Weird edge-case: sequential shot-order sensitivity
- Shuffling exemplar order changes outputs dramatically for some queries. Not linear with similarity; sometimes switching EX2 and EX3 flips answer style. Suspect model attention ranking heuristics + position encoding interactions.
- Quick experiment plan: systematically permute 3-exemplar banks (6 permutations) and compute pairwise answer similarity. Add to backlog if variance > threshold.

Quick prompts I want to keep/try in harness
- "Extract bullets from the text. If the text doesn't say it, write '— not stated'"
- Short provenance: "For each bullet, add '(source: [sentence index])'"
- Fewshot format to try: label-answer-provenance triple, with provenance as sentence-number not free text.

Open questions / To triage
- Does adding explicit sentence indices reduce invented sources? (A/B test)
- Can we make negative examples more operational (showing error) rather than advisory?
- How bad is exemplar order sensitivity across model sizes (tiny, base, large)?

Todo (next 2 weeks)
- Convert minimal repro snippets into small unit tests for the harness (JIRA: DX-1987).
- Run exemplar permutation sweep for 3-exemplar banks (script: prompt-gizmo/sweep-v1).
- Try provenance-as-index approach across 3 models (quantify hallucination delta).
- Draft a short internal note with recommendations for Product docs (/dx/integration-guide) on fewshot pitfalls.

Random salvage notes (brain-dump)
- Use emojis in UI only when you want a stylistic nudge; they are too fuzzy for reliability tests.
- 'If unsure, ask clarifying Q' sometimes causes the model to hallucinate a clarifying question that presumes facts. Better: force clarifying as options checkboxes in UI.
- Keep short negative examples (<12 words) else they become interpreted as a policy restatement.

References and linked quick artifacts
- GH: prompt-gizmo-experiments/README (scripts + sample outputs)
- JIRA DX-1987: capture minimal repros and assign engineering triage
- Confluence draft: "Fewshot gotchas and quick mitigations" (link above)

Notes to future me (Priya)
- If you revisit this in >6 months, check whether "position sensitivity" changed after runtime kernel updates — there was a kernel PR that touched tokenization ordering in mid-2024.
- Save a snapshot of the final best-performing prompt as a pinned exemplar in the harness; don't rely on memory.

End of log.

(If collaborating: leave quick comments in the GH PR or add inline notes — this doc is intentionally messy)
